title: Home Mortgage Loans: how a payment posts and is applied
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: how a payment posts and is applied

This policy governs every borrower payment on Home Mortgage Loans: which loans can accept a payment, what a full installment is, what happens to a short payment, and in what order a payment is applied.

## Policy clauses

1. **Loans that accept payments.** Payments post only to a loan whose status is active, delinquent or forbearance. The status is read from the bank's record of the loan the payment is for.
2. **Full installment.** A full installment is the monthly principal and interest payment plus the monthly escrow payment.
3. **Short payments.** A payment smaller than one full installment is handled under the program's partial payment handling and is returned to the borrower without being applied.
4. **Order within an installment.** Each full installment is applied to interest, then to principal, then to escrow.
5. **Amount beyond whole installments.** Any amount beyond whole installments is applied first to fees due, which are unpaid late charges and servicing fees, and then, when it is at least the program's smallest extra principal payment, to principal as a curtailment.
6. **Late charges and installments.** Late charges are never deducted from an installment, so a timely full installment is never made late by an unpaid late charge.
7. **Prepayment.** No prepayment penalty applies.
8. **Paying from checking.** A payment made from a PCB checking account is debited from that checking account.

## Input, judgement and output (hypothetical loan)

Hypothetical loan: monthly principal and interest of 1100.00 and monthly escrow of 400.00, so one full installment is 1500.00; fees due of 60.00.

| Payment received | Judgement | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 1400.00 | Smaller than one full installment | Returned to the borrower, not applied |
| 1500.00 | One whole installment, nothing beyond | Applied to interest, then principal, then escrow; the 60.00 fees due stay unpaid |
| 3000.00 | Two whole installments | Each installment applied to interest, then principal, then escrow |
| 2000.00 | One whole installment and 500.00 beyond | 1500.00 to the installment; of the 500.00, 60.00 to fees due, and the remaining 440.00 to principal as a curtailment provided 440.00 is at least the program's smallest extra principal payment |

## Status check (hypothetical loans)

| Loan status on record | Can a payment post? |
|---|---|
| Active | Yes |
| Delinquent | Yes |
| Forbearance | Yes |
| Applied, withdrawn or paid off | No |

## Basis Q&A

- **Can a borrower's installment be treated as short because a late charge is outstanding?** No. Late charges are never deducted from an installment; a timely full installment is never made late by an unpaid late charge.
- **Does paying the loan down early cost a penalty?** No prepayment penalty applies.
- **Hypothetical case.** A borrower with an unpaid late charge of 50.00 pays exactly 1500.00, one full installment, on time. The whole 1500.00 is applied to the installment, the installment is not late, and the 50.00 late charge remains in fees due.
